questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. Which equation defines the price-break indifference quantity $Q$?

In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. The equation $TCU_2(y)=TCU_1(y_m)$ has two positive roots. Why is the indifference quantity $Q$ the larger one?
options: Both roots solve $TCU_2(y)=TCU_1(y_m)$, so either may be used
The smaller root lies below $y_m$, where $y_m$ itself already qualifies
The smaller root is always negative, so it is no batch size $y>0$
At the larger root the net saving over $TCU_1(y_m)$ is largest

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. Why is there exactly one batch size $Q>y_m$ with $TCU_2(Q)=TCU_1(y_m)$?
options: Because $TCU_2$ is constant beyond $y_m$, so equality holds on a whole interval
Because the two curves cross once, at the threshold $q$ chosen by the supplier
Because a solution exists only when the discount $c_1-c_2$ is large enough
Because $TCU_2(y_m)<TCU_1(y_m)$ and $TCU_2$ rises without bound beyond $y_m$

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. A student calls $Q$ 'the EOQ at the discounted price $c_2$'. What is wrong with this?
options: $Q$ is a comparison threshold; $TCU_2$ is not stationary there
$Q$ is in fact the EOQ at price $c_1$, not at price $c_2$
$Q$ is the optimal order whenever a discount is offered
$Q$ equals $y_m$, since $h$ is the same at both prices

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. A supplier sets the threshold $q<y_m$. What role does the indifference quantity $Q$ play in the ordering decision?
options: Order exactly $q$, the smallest batch that gets price $c_2$
None: $y_m$ already qualifies, so order $y_m$ at price $c_2$
Compare $q$ with $Q$ first, and order $q$ only if $q<Q$
Order $Q$, the largest batch that is still worth the discount

Given the indifference quantity $Q=200$, which batch should be bought when the discount needs at least $q=250$ units?

With $TCU_1(y_m)=500$, the indifference quantity solves $Q^2+bQ+\frac{2KD}{h}=0$ with $b=\frac{2(c_2D-TCU_1(y_m))}{h}$. What is $b$?
For an all-unit price break with $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}=100$, the equation $TCU_2(Q)=TCU_1(y_m)$ becomes $Q^2-250Q+10000=0$. What is the indifference quantity $Q$?

What is the cost level $TCU_1(y_m)$ per week that the discounted cost must match at the indifference quantity?

In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. Why is $TCU_2(Q)$ set equal to $TCU_1(y_m)$ rather than to $TCU_1(Q)$?
options: Because $y_m$ at price $c_1$ is the best option without discount
Because $TCU_1(Q)$ and $TCU_1(y_m)$ are equal for every batch size $Q$
Because $TCU_2(y_m)$ is not defined when $y_m$ is below the threshold
Because a batch of size $Q$ is bought at price $c_1$ as well

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. The supplier increases the discount by lowering $c_2$, while $c_1$, $K$, $D$ and $h$ stay fixed. How does the indifference quantity $Q$ change?
options: It falls, since a cheaper unit price makes holding stock cheaper
It stays the same, since $y_m$ does not depend on any price
It moves to $y_m$, since the discounted EOQ then changes
It rises, so a wider band of thresholds becomes worth meeting

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. Why does every threshold $q$ with $y_m<q<Q$ make ordering $q$ strictly cheaper than ordering $y_m$ at price $c_1$?
options: Because $q$ is the EOQ of the discounted cost curve $TCU_2$
Because purchasing cost at $q$ is lower, whatever setup and holding cost
Because $TCU_1$ is convex, so $TCU_1(q)<TCU_1(y_m)$ for such $q$

questions.question: Annual demand is $D=1000$, setup cost $K=20$ per order and holding cost $h=4$ per unit per year, so $y_m=100$. Units cost 10, or 9.55 for batches of at least $q$ units (all-unit discount). What is the indifference quantity $Q$?

For this case the indifference quantity is $Q=200$. Both prices then rise by 1, to 3 and 2.875. What is the new indifference quantity?

Solving $TCU_2(y)=TCU_1(100)$ gives the roots 50 and 200. A student takes $Q=50$ and, for the threshold $q=120$, keeps ordering 100 units at price 2. What is the correct decision?

In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. The equation $TCU_2(y)=TCU_1(y_m)$ has roots $Q>y_m$ and a smaller root $Q'$. Using the quadratic $y^2+by+2KD/h=0$, how is $Q'$ related to $Q$?
options: $Q'=y_m/Q$, the ratio of the EOQ $y_m$ to $Q$

questions.question: In the EOQ model with an all-unit price break (demand $D$, setup cost $K$, holding cost $h$ at both prices, unit price $c_1$ below the threshold $q$ and $c_2<c_1$ from $q$ on), let $TCU_j(y)=Dc_j+KD/y+hy/2$ and $y_m=\sqrt{2KD/h}$. For a threshold $q>y_m$, how is the condition $q<Q$ related to 'ordering $q$ is strictly cheaper than ordering $y_m$ at price $c_1$'?
options: It guarantees the saving, but the saving can occur without it
It guarantees the saving and is also required for that saving
It is required for the saving, but does not guarantee it
It neither guarantees the saving nor is required for it
